highlights.title: Williams and Alcaraz reach mixed doubles quarters before exit
highlights.summary: Star pairing Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles before being beaten by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
body: Williams - a 23-time Grand Slam singles champion - returned to tennis in June at the age of 44 and secured her first professional win since 2022 as she and Alcaraz beat Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and partner Erin Routliffe in their opening match.

It was also seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first match back on tour after a wrist injury sidelined the reigning men's singles champion since April. The 22-year-old was born five years after Williams won the 1998 mixed doubles title at Flushing Meadows.
The dynamic pairing bounced back from a slow start to claim a 5-3 4-1 opening victory over Routliffe and Glasspool, much to the delight of fans inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
"I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

highlights.title: 'The Dog Stars Review: Ridley Scott's New Sci-Fi Odyssey Is an Action Movie Like No Other
highlights.summary: Quiet, contemplative moments like these keep The Dog Stars grounded and accessible throughout its sprawling post-apocalyptic story — even as director Ridley Scott piles on epic action set pieces and surreal, surprising sequences that sometimes push the film from prestige drama into absurdist…
body: Hig pilots his small, vintage plane up into the Colorado mountains, cuts the engine, and glides. Surrounded by endless sky and soft green forest, there’s a look of uneasy peace on the young man’s face. Serenity, grief, and a glimmer of a death wish swirl together against the canvas of Jacob Elordi’s perpetual 5 o'clock shadow as he soars silently through the air, waiting until the last possible minute to restart the engine and fly back home.

In The Dog Stars, based on the 2012 book of the same name by Peter Heller and adapted by screenwriter Mark L. Smith ( The Revenant ), Elordi’s Hig is one of the few remaining survivors on Earth, years after a deadly virus swept the planet. He lives on an old airfield with a former marine named Bangley (Josh Brolin). All things considered, they have a pretty good life — plenty of whiskey, cigarettes, bullets, and the safety of a secure perimeter — but Hig wants something more.

highlights.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
highlights.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.

highlights.title: My pup Koopa and I put 15 dog beds to the test – these are ones that survived
highlights.summary: We tried models from Black Lab, K9 Ballistics, Orvis, Znooz and others to find beds that were long-lasting, washable, and most of all, comfortable. The best dog harnesses and dog toys – pup-tested. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: While our four-legged best friends are often happy enough to sprawl on the floor or curl up on an old blanket, there’s an increasing number of companies out there making plush and durable spots for pampered pups to lie.

But given the destructive tendencies of some dogs and that some of these beds cost well into the hundreds of dollars, buying the wrong one can quickly turn into an expensive mess. We tested 15 different models to find the best for every situation.

I’ve tested everything from sports cars to smartphones for dozens of international outlets since the late 90s, but I’ve been a dog owner and lover my entire life. For the Filter, my pups and I have put dog harnesses and dog toys to the test. Along the way, my pups have curled up on everything from leftover couch cushions to high-grade beds from big-brand stores.
I’ve seen which types of beds work and which fall apart, which are easy to take apart and which are a real struggle and which stand up best to repeated cleaning and drying cycles.

highlights.title: The world's busiest spaceport is about to get a lot quieter, at least for now
highlights.summary: SpaceX made Florida's Space Coast home to the world's busiest spaceport for a decade, but that will change this year. The company is significantly cutting the number of launches from Florida until Starship arrives, a senior SpaceX official confirmed Tuesday.
body: The Falcon 9 rocket has been SpaceX’s workhorse, routinely launching batches of satellites for the company’s Starlink network, primarily from launch pads at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. There were 165 Falcon 9 launches last year—about three flights per week—and about 75 percent of them carried Starlink satellites.

This year is different. SpaceX has launched more missions from its West Coast launch pad at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California since January, and this trend will amplify for the rest of the year.

A Falcon 9 launch early Tuesday was the last planned Starlink mission from Cape Canaveral until SpaceX begins flying Starship missions from Florida, according to Kiko Dontchev, the company’s vice president of launch. For at least the rest of the year, and maybe longer, this means the launch rate at the Florida spaceport will drop from eight or nine per month to perhaps two per month.

highlights.title: OpenAI loses a top data center exec, as stream of high-profile departures continues
highlights.summary: Before Malone left, OpenAI had already reshuffled its infrastructure org, shifting his reporting line away from President Greg Brockman and putting Vice President Sachin Katti in charge of the group.
body: OpenAI has lost yet another executive, and the timing of this one stands out in particular given this individual oversaw the execution of the company’s data center strategy.

Chris Malone, OpenAI’s former head of data centers, left the company last week, the Wall Street Journal has reported. Malone, who spent nearly five years at Meta and more than a decade at Google before that, joined OpenAI in March of last year, making his tenure relatively short.

Malone joined the company not long after the launch of the Stargate Project, a $500 million data center initiative championed by the Trump administration that has sought to develop data centers in the U.S. OpenAI, along with Oracle, Nvidia, SoftBank and Microsoft, is considered a key partner in the effort.

Why is Malone leaving? It’s isn’t entirely clear. With the AI infrastructure buildout frenzy in full swing across the industry, data center strategy has become one of the most closely watched roles at any AI lab, which makes turnover in that seat especially surprising.

New Zealand fielded only three players from that Saturday Test victory over South Africa on the same ground and involved five injury replacements summoned on tour - including one who arrived on Monday - as well as giving a debut to prop Saula Ma'u.
Their defence struggled and missed 19 tackles over the course of the contest that saw them trail 14-0 after seven minutes.

They were still behind at half-time and 35-17 behind in the 47th minute, as the Lions threatened to become the first South African provincial side to beat New Zealand since Orange Free State, now known as the Cheetahs, in 1976.

highlights.title: Steam's Most Intriguing Slow-Burn Adventure Game Takes 400 Real-World Days to Finish
highlights.summary: Somewhere on your hard drive, a small, wide-eyed creature named Shade will keep standing alone in the dark, waiting on a ticking timer to go down, whether you’re there, watching as well, or not.
body: The intimacy this game offers is both eerie and surreal. You’ll find yourself with a new appreciation for your surroundings and how they shift over time. The “idle” half of the game does precisely what it promises: Assign Shade a task, close the game entirely, and, next time you check in, whether it’s a day or a month later, he’ll have completed it. Keep the game open while you’re accomplishing other things in your real-life space, and Shade will sit down on the cave floor and keep you company, occasionally muttering to himself about the water dripping nearby.

As one might expect for a unique game like this, the reception is mixed. Steam’s reviews for it currently sit at a Very Positive, and many people absolutely love this game. Some even restart the whole 400-day clock from scratch after drifting away for too long, unable to shake the feeling that they'd abandoned Shade and couldn’t simply pick back up where they left off. Others wonder what the point of this game is. One critic called The Longing “ Animal Crossing: Depressing Edition.” Depending on who you are and what you’re looking for in a gaming experience, that could be a compliment or a warning label. Your choice.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.

highlights.title: OpenAI says its Jalapeño chip can power faster AI responses than the competition
highlights.summary: OpenAI says its new AI chip, Jalapeño, completes tasks more efficiently and returns responses faster than other AI systems, according to a blog post published on Tuesday.
body: First introduced in June, Jalapeño is an Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) made in partnership with Broadcom. It’s designed for AI inference — the process of running a trained AI model to complete a task or deploy an agent.

To measure Jalapeño’s performance, OpenAI used InferenceX, a benchmarking platform that shows how well AI systems handle inference. The test compared Jalapeño’s performance against the best results recorded at the time, which were with Nvidia’s GB200 or GB300 superchips. OpenAI says Jalapeño delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1, and Kimi K2.5 1T than the comparison systems, while offering 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency across the three models. That means the chip can provide users with “faster responses, more responsive agents, and more reliable access as the demand grows,” according to Ho.

OpenAI plans to deploy Jalapeño in “small volumes” by the end of this year, but will begin to “ramp the volume up” into 2027, Ho added. The company doesn’t say how many chips it plans to deploy next year, however.

highlights.title: The 5 Most Unforgettable Moments of Critical Role Campaign 4 So Far
highlights.summary: Critical Role Campaign 4 has been an emotional rollercoaster since it debuted in October 2025. There have been epic battles, incredible game-shattering moments, shenanigans involving bikinis made out of souls, and, as expected in a Dungeons & Dragons campaign, plenty of death.
body: To celebrate Arc 2 of Campaign 4 set to premiere this Thursday night, we’ve rounded up five of the best, biggest, and wildest moments of Campaign 4 so far.
Critical Role had an overwhelming number of shocking moments in its four-episode overture, so narrowing it down to one big thing was difficult.

The arrival of House Tachonis assassins at Palazzo Davinos and their brutal slaughter of the households of House Royce, Davinos, and Occtis Tachonis ( who, don’t worry, recovered) kept us on the edge of our seats from beginning to end. With the players still low-level, Critters unsure which player character would even survive into the next arc, and the constant reminder that “anyone could die,” this moment established a Game of Thrones -like tone that has persisted throughout the campaign.

The death of Thjazi Fang, the character who brought the 13 characters together in the first place, occurred after he got sold out by one of his old war buddies, Crow Keeper Casimir Gavendale. As a reward for his effort, he was granted the title of Baron of Sloak.

highlights.title: How to Party Like a Local in Mykonos, According to a Seasoned Veteran
highlights.summary: A lifelong regular’s guide to choosing the right coast, landing in the part of the venue you meant to book, and getting home before the taxis disappear.
body: The sun starts to set on Little Venice and its windmills in Mykonos Town, one of many popular vistas on the island.

Now craft beer is brewed on the island, and casual Chora bars pour proper cocktails into paper cups and send revelers off into the night. Greek musicians share the calendar with international DJs, periodically reminding Mykonos of which country it belongs to. The familiar bottle-service caricature leaves out the drag stages of the old port and the smaller rooms where a night can change direction without a reservation. Prices remain high and the roads maddening, but few Mediterranean islands offer so many convincing ways to reach sunrise. After enough summers on both sides of the nap, I have settled on seven rules that every visitor needs to know.
Many of the outdoor tables in Little Venice are just inches from the tide.

highlights.title: ‘Darth Vader’ Wants You to Know He Definitely Supports Flock Surveillance
highlights.summary: Anthony Ralphs was frustrated by the San Diego City Council's support for Flock. He decided it would take something more than reasoned argument to get their attention.
body: At the San Diego City Council’s most recent budget meeting, Sith Lord Darth Vader had some points to make. Between gasping breaths, Vader praised the council’s recent votes to renew its contract with the surveillance company Flock Safety, which has been making headlines recently as more and more stories of police officers abusing its tools have continued to come out—and as a WIRED review of code for a new AI tool already in use by some police departments has made clear that it is watching far more than just license plates.

“The emperor is a fan of Flock. And we must continue utilizing Flock technologies so that we can follow and surveil the rebel scum as they move from playground to playground, from playground to pool, from pool to gymnasium.”
The recording of the video has gone viral, reaching millions of people on TikTok and Instagram.

The man behind the stunt is Anthony Ralphs, a San Diego-based DJ, event producer, and agriculture consultant who has spent the better part of the past year advocating against the city’s support of Flock’s use by the San Diego Police Department.

highlights.title: Claude Cowork finally remembers what you told the app in chat
highlights.summary: Anthropic is giving Claude a shared memory across chat and Cowork, so users no longer have to repeatedly brief the AI on projects, preferences, and other context.
body: A change to Claude’s memory system will eliminate one of the most annoying things about using agents — the constant need to rebrief the AI on things it already knows. On Tuesday, Anthropic announced it’s merging the memory system used by chat and Claude Cowork, which means that Claude will always remember what it learned in one area, even when you’re engaging with it in another.
Anthropic is also exposing what Claude has retained in its memory, allowing users to read, edit, or delete information on any topic.
The update will improve the experience for Claude’s users as it will allow them to more seamlessly move between the research phase and taking action.

Before, you may have developed ideas for projects over time while chatting with Claude, but when it came time to actually enact the changes, you’d have to start over by telling Cowork all the details. This was incredibly frustrating. The update makes Claude now feel like one continuous assistant, rather than two separate products under one roof.

“I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry and skating can evolve,” Liu wrote. “It’s important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth.”

highlights.summary: Viral videos of the World Humanoid Robot Games show sprinting robots beating the human 100-meter record held by Usain Bolt—but also feature running robots crashing into barriers and falling down because they cannot readily stop running.
body: That demonstration of both robotic prowess and limitations came from the second edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games hosted in Beijing from August 22–26. Like the inaugural event held in 2025, this year’s event challenged humanoid robots to run fast, perform kung fu or dance moves, fight one another in kickboxing, and play soccer or table tennis.

This year’s games also tested robots in more humdrum practical scenarios like washing and hanging laundry, where they appeared to lag behind typical human working speeds. That suggests the event organizers, including Chinese state media and the Beijing city government, are keen to showcase the commercial potential of humanoid robots at a time when China’s robotics industry is rapidly developing and testing such robots.

The fact that humanoid robots went from lagging behind human record-holders last year to surpassing human world records in the 100-meter sprint and standing high jump events this year suggests significant progress in robotic whole-body control for accomplishing specific tasks, Dipam Patel, a PhD candidate in computer science at Purdue University and a research assistant at the US Army DevCom Army Research Lab, told Ars.

highlights.title: People’s bodies are changing in the age of Ozempic. How are we meant to talk about it?
highlights.summary: Discussing people’s bodies can be fraught. We asked eating disorder experts how to do so – or not – responsibly. In the age of Ozempic and people being open about plastic surgery, discussion about people’s bodies is rife.
body: It is a fraught topic. We asked eating disorder experts for guidelines to follow when talking about other people’s bodies, and how to do so without doing harm.

For experts in the field of eating disorders, the current ambivalence makes sense. “There’s a whiplash moment we’re stuck in,” says Dr Tom Hildebrandt, director of the Center for Eating and Weight Disorders at Mount Sinai hospital in New York.

The body positivity movement of the 2010s saw a mainstream push to “accept all body sizes, shapes and types”, says Hildebrandt. Then, with the explosion of GLP-1s, progress toward body acceptance “took a hard right turn”, he says – once again, “the media went through its idealization of weight loss”.
The vocabulary is different than it was before. Now, the focus is on “optimizing” one’s body and appearance, says Dr Ulrike Schmidt, professor of eating disorders at King’s College London.

highlights.title: After 25 Years, Sci-fi Cult Classic Donnie Darko is Officially Getting a Proper Sequel
highlights.summary: Few movies have inspired as much late-night theorizing as Donnie Darko. Richard Kelly’s 2001 cult classic follows Donnie, a troubled teenager who begins seeing visions of Frank, a stranger in a sinister bunny costume who warns him that the world will end in 28 days.
body: Even after multiple viewings, Donnie Darko remains difficult to fully decode — and if anyone tells you they understand it fully, they're probably lying. That's part of why the film has maintained such a devoted following. Now, 25 years after the film’s release, Kelly is preparing to revisit that strange world.

As first reported by Variety, writer-director Richard Kelly is releasing a sequel book, The Philosophy of Time Travel, later this year. The approximately 800-page novel will be published by Range Literary Publishing and is expected to arrive in the fourth quarter, around the film’s 25th anniversary.

The book picks up 14 months after Donnie’s death and will be told through found documents, including material written from the perspectives of Donnie’s parents, Rose and Eddie. The story will follow the characters as they try to understand what happened to Donnie, the tangent universe and the strange events they collectively experienced.

highlights.title: It Should Be Harder to Apply for a Job. No, Really
highlights.summary: Thanks to a dwindling supply of open roles, “one-click” applications, and the rise of artificial intelligence, it’s easier than ever to apply for a job. We’re all paying the price.
body: Three years ago, Andrew Stockwell had his hiring routine down to a science.

As head of people for the software-buying company Vendr, Stockwell posted a listing, waited a few days, and then reviewed a few dozen applications—up to 100, if he was lucky. Recruiters identified other potential candidates, adding a few more applicants to the mix. Stockwell read résumés, conducted interviews, and passed along sterling candidates to hiring managers.
“It was really about finding that great talent, sussing out that talent, speaking with that talent, and identifying the best possible people,” Stockwell tells WIRED.

Stockwell is one of many recruitment professionals who believe looking for a job is fundamentally broken. In 2026, job hunting has become as easy as online shopping: AI can crank out tailored résumés and cover letters in seconds. Browser extensions can autofill applications, no human necessary. LinkedIn serves users dozens of jobs a day, many with the option to apply with “just a few clicks.”
